title: Graceful Shutdown with WaitGroup Drain
description:
**Problem**: `engine.go` `Stop()` cancels context but doesn't wait for in-flight `HandlePacket` goroutines. Jobs mid-dispatch get abandoned — lock held but goroutine dead, zombie state until lock TTL (30s).

**Fix**:
- Add `sync.WaitGroup` to Engine struct
- `wg.Add(1)` at start of each `HandlePacket`, `defer wg.Done()`
- `Stop()`: cancel context, then `wg.Wait()` with 10s deadline
- Log warning if drain exceeds deadline

**Files**: `core/controlplane/scheduler/engine.go`
definitionOfDone: Stop() waits for in-flight goroutines with 10s deadline
Warning logged if drain exceeds deadline
New test: Stop() waits for in-flight handlers

implementationPlan.description:
Step 1: Add sync.WaitGroup to Engine struct and initialize in NewEngine

In `core/controlplane/scheduler/engine.go`:
- Add `wg sync.WaitGroup` field to the Engine struct (line 37-49)
- Import `sync` if not already present (already imported via `sync/atomic`)
- No change needed in NewEngine — zero-value WaitGroup is ready to use
implementationPlan.note: Added `sync` import and `wg sync.WaitGroup` field to Engine struct. Zero-value WaitGroup is ready to use.

implementationPlan.description:
Step 2: Track HandlePacket goroutines with wg.Add/Done

In `engine.go` `HandlePacket()` (line 139), add at the very top after nil/stopped checks:
```go
e.wg.Add(1)
defer e.wg.Done()
```
This must go AFTER the `e.stopped.Load()` check (line 143) so we don't track handlers that will immediately return nil.
implementationPlan.note: Added wg.Add(1)/defer wg.Done() after the stopped check, before the payload switch. Handlers that arrive after Stop() sets stopped=true are rejected before Add, so no leak.
Replaced Stop(): sets stopped=true first (rejects new packets), then cancels context, then waits for wg with 10s deadline. Logs warning if drain exceeds deadline.

implementationPlan.description:
Step 4: Add test TestStopWaitsForInflightHandlers

In engine_test.go, add a test that:
1. Creates engine with a slow-publishing fakeBus (adds a `time.Sleep(200ms)` in Publish)
2. Starts handling a job in a goroutine
3. Calls Stop() immediately after
4. Asserts Stop() blocks for at least ~200ms (handler completes)
5. Asserts handler completed successfully (job state is RUNNING)
implementationPlan.note: Added TestStopWaitsForInflightHandlers: uses slowBus with 200ms Publish delay, starts HandlePacket in goroutine, calls Stop() immediately, asserts Stop() blocks for at least 100ms (proving it waited for the in-flight handler). Also verifies handler goroutine completed.

implementationPlan.description: Step 5: Verify all tests pass with `go test ./core/controlplane/scheduler/... -count=3`
implementationPlan.note: All tests pass with -count=3 (1.892s). Fixed minor compile error (removed non-existent MaxJobs field from Heartbeat proto literal).
